state: I confess I very nearly retched when the chemist unwrapped that weeping blister on my heel for all the queue to see; a most revolting spectacle before breakfast.

Upon returning from my morning walk, I was met at the garden gate by a face I had not glimpsed in twenty years: my nephew Edmund, apparently now residing at number fourteen. I confess I stood rooted to the pavement, quite unable to form a sentence for a full minute. The Hendersons, it transpires, sold the house without a word to any of us along the lane. One does not expect such a turn after two decades of familiar faces next door.

- Front row, close enough to feel the bass in my ribs
- Sang until my voice cracked, worth every second

The power went out around seven, right as the wind started doing that thing where it makes the whole house sound like it's clearing its throat. My first thought, obviously, was to complain about it to nobody in particular, because that's the job of a homeowner during a storm. Candles came out. Then the good flashlight, then the bad flashlight that only works if you hold it at a very specific angle like you're divining for water. My sister-in-law, who I usually only see at forced holiday gatherings, was stuck here for the night because the bridge road floods, and within twenty minutes we had dug out a deck of cards missing the seven of clubs and were three rounds into a game we kept making up rules for as we went. The dog thought the thunder was a personal insult and wedged himself between us on the couch, which nobody complained about. We ended up staying up until past one, telling the kind of stories you only tell when there's nothing else to do and no phone to check, and at some point I caught myself laughing hard enough that my ribs hurt over a joke that, retold in daylight, will almost certainly not be funny. By the time the lights flickered back on, somebody groaned. I did not say what I was thinking, which was that I wouldn't have minded if they'd stayed off a while longer.

ok so remember how i said the layover in Millbridge was gonna be fine bc it was 3 hours. cool. cool cool cool. bc apparently 3 hours is not enough time when your first flight sits on the tarmac for 40 min for 'de-icing' and then the gate for the SECOND flight changes THREE times and each time it's like a 15 min walk to the new one. i sprinted through B concourse with my backpack bouncing off my spine like a maraca, got to the new gate with 4 min to spare, and the guy just. closes the door. in my face. while i am standing RIGHT THERE. he looks at me, looks at the screen, and says 'doors close at departure time' like that's a normal thing to say to a person who is visibly still moving. so now i get to spend 6 hours in this airport eating a $14 pretzel out of spite, and when i called the airline the hold music looped through the same 30 seconds of smooth jazz for 45 minutes before a bot told me to 'try the app.' the app that has been stuck on 'loading your trip' since Tuesday. i'm not even asking for a refund at this point i just want someone at that company to say the words 'that was our fault' one single time. lower your expectations they said. travel builds character they said.

Credit where due: it was one of the best matches I've sat through in years. Down two goals at half, some kind of tactical miracle in the second half, then an equalizer in second-half stoppage time that had the entire section on its feet screaming like we'd personally scored it. I will remember the noise in that stadium for a long time. What I will also remember, unfortunately, is the man three seats down who spent the entire second half working through a family-sized bag of nacho fries and using the empty seat between us as, near as I could tell, a napkin, a bin, and at one point a foot rest, cheese sauce and all. Somewhere around the eightieth minute he leaned over, genuinely, mid-celebration, arms still in the air, to ask if I was 'gonna finish that,' meaning my drink, which he then picked up without waiting for an answer and drank from directly. I watched him do it. I said nothing, because what is there to say, but I have not been able to think about that cup since, and I definitely didn't finish it after. The goal was incredible. The comeback was the stuff of local legend, the kind of thing people will bring up unprompted for the rest of the season. I just need everyone to also know there was a man there treating a stranger's game-day snacks like community property, cheese sauce and all, and I have not recovered.

packed up the last box today. stood in the empty living room for a minute bc it doesnt even echo the same without the furniture. 12 years in this house and it just looks like any other empty room now. gonna miss the mark on the doorframe where we measured the kids every birthday, new place doesnt have that. hard not to cry loading the truck tbh

After reading the screenshots of what she'd actually written about me to the group, forwarded by someone who thought I needed to see it, I scrubbed my phone screen like it had touched something rotten.

Oh totally, I'm not lying awake running through every single way tomorrow's presentation could go wrong, definitely not doing that! Who even needs sleep when you've got three hours of catastrophic what-if scenarios queued up and ready to play on a loop? Super chill over here, honestly, zero notes, everything's fine, my hands are just cold for no reason at all!

Filing this here mostly so I remember never to use the shared break room fridge again:
- Opened it to grab my lunch and found a container in the back that has clearly not been touched since before the holidays, the lid bulging upward like it's trying to escape.
- Someone left a half-eaten yogurt directly on the shelf, no lid, just sitting open next to everyone else's food, growing something with visible texture.
- The 'FREE FOOD' box by the microwave had a plate of unidentifiable meat sitting out at room temperature since at least Tuesday, based on the sticky note underneath it.
- Microwave interior has a permanent orange splatter ring baked onto the ceiling of it that nobody, in the four years I've worked here, has ever wiped off.
- Sink drain was fully clogged with what I am choosing to describe only as 'organic matter,' and someone had just kept running water into it anyway, so now there's standing grey water pooling around three unwashed mugs.
- I opened the trash can lid to throw away a napkin and audibly gagged, closed it, and left the napkin on the counter instead.
Sent an email to facilities with photos attached. I do not know how to caption a photo of a bulging Tupperware in a way that conveys the appropriate level of urgency, but I tried. Bringing my lunch in a cooler bag from now on and eating at my desk like a normal, sanitary person.

Took one bite of the soup, chewed exactly once, and set my spoon down very deliberately next to the bowl like it had personally wronged me. Pushed the bowl about six inches to the left, which is apparently as far as my arm was willing to commit to the problem. Ordered plain toast instead and didn't look at the soup again for the rest of the meal. The waiter asked if everything was okay and I just gestured at the bowl the way you'd point out a small fire.

Our old spaniel, Barnaby, did not touch his supper again this evening, the third night running, and has taken to trembling under the hall table whenever I so much as reach for his lead. I lay awake a good while last night dreading what the vet might tell us come Monday morning. He is fourteen years old, and I am not sure my nerves can bear much more of this waiting.
Lost power for two days, no big deal, but the old oak out back didn't survive the wind, and now there's just a stump where thirty years of tree forts used to be.

Preparations were, admittedly, meticulous: two tickets secured in the presale window, parking pre-booked, the setlist from the last tour cross-referenced against likely encore choices. All of that planning was for a trip Marlene and I had scheduled fourteen months ago, before her diagnosis changed the timeline for everything. I used the second ticket tonight, seat B14, empty beside me for the full two hours. The band played the song we'd argued over which of us loved more. I still don't have an answer for that argument, and now I never will.

Opened up the old laptop to clean the fans and found the keyboard tray coated in a layer of crumbs fused together with something sticky I can't identify. Three dead gnats under the trackpad. A single hair, not mine, wedged into the space bar mechanism. Wiped it all down twice and still don't want to touch the thing barehanded.

There's a meeting on the calendar for Thursday at 2pm titled simply 'Team Update,' no agenda attached, organized directly by the VP rather than our usual manager, which is already unusual enough to have noticed, and I have now noticed it roughly forty times since Monday morning. I've been trying to build a case in my head for why this is nothing: maybe it's about the new expense software, maybe it's a routine reorg announcement that has nothing to do with headcount, maybe I'm reading tea leaves in an empty cup. But then I remember that Priya's badge stopped working on Tuesday and nobody has mentioned why, and that the shared drive got a new folder called 'Q3 Transition Docs' that none of us have access to, and that my manager has rescheduled our one-on-one twice this week with no real explanation either time. I keep rehearsing, uselessly, what I would say if it comes to that: about the mortgage renewal in October, about whether my health coverage would run out mid-month or end-of-month, about how long severance conversations even take before you know numbers. I looked up our state's unemployment filing process last night at eleven, which is not a normal thing to do on a Tuesday, and then closed the tab and told myself I was being dramatic. I haven't said any of this to my partner yet because saying it out loud makes the Thursday meeting feel like a fact instead of a guess, and right now it is still, technically, just a meeting with a vague title on a calendar I keep refreshing like it might tell me something new.
Doctor looked at the scan, looked at me, and said 'well, I've got nothing to fix,' which is the first time in three years a specialist has sent me home with literally no follow-up appointment.

Ever since I heard she's been telling other people I 'ditched' her, I've drafted four different replies to her last text and deleted every one before sending, checking her online status more than I'd like to admit.
Third time this month he's brought up the two hundred dollars I lent him only to change the subject the second I ask when he can pay it back.

Insurance denied Mason's inhaler refill for the second time this year calling it 'not medically necessary' and I have now spent three lunch breaks on hold with a company that has never once met my asthmatic six year old.

so the 'boutique hostel' photos were... doing a lot of heavy lifting. got there and the sheets had a stain that was definitely not part of the pattern, there was a full on trail of ants going into the minifridge, and the bathroom drain smelled like it had personally given up on life. asked for new sheets and the guy just flipped them over and handed them back like that solved anything. slept in my hoodie on top of my own towel, did not touch a single surface barefoot the whole time.
Final headcount approval came through this morning: I start as team lead on the fourteenth, with budget sign-off for the two hires I'd been requesting since January.

Spent most of last night convinced I'd somehow failed statistics badly enough to need a whole extra semester, the kind of spiral where you start mentally rearranging your entire five-year plan around one exam. Portal opened at 8am. Refreshed it maybe six times before it actually loaded. Turns out I didn't just pass, I pulled the second-highest grade in a class of ninety, which is a sentence I have now read back to myself an embarrassing number of times just to make sure it's real. Already told my mother twice. Might tell the mailman next.

I shall confess at the outset that I hold very little patience for these modern telephone contraptions, and my exchange with the young man at the broadband company's helpline did nothing to improve my opinion of the matter; I was transferred four times, made to repeat my account number on each occasion, and left on hold to a recording of what I can only describe as saxophone music for the better part of forty minutes. I mention this only so that what follows may be properly appreciated. Having given up entirely on the telephone, I asked my grandson, Oliver, to simply 'have a look' at the router himself when he called round on Sunday. He was finished, by the clock on my mantel, in under four minutes, without once dialling a single number or raising his voice to anyone. When I asked how on earth he had managed what an entire call centre could not, he showed me a small screen on his own telephone displaying what he called a 'diagnostic,' as though the router itself had simply told him, in its own language, precisely what was the matter with it. I sat down rather heavily in my armchair afterward. Sixty years I have lived alongside telephones, wirelesses, and now these little glowing boxes in every room, and I confess I had never once considered that a machine might report its own ailments the way a patient describes symptoms to a doctor. Oliver seemed to find my astonishment rather funny. I have been turning the whole business over in my mind ever since, and I still cannot quite settle on what to make of it.

opened the mail today and there was a letter from a great aunt i didnt even know existed, turns out my grandad had a whole other sister nobody in the family ever mentioned. called my mom and she didnt know either. still dont really know what to do with that info tbh, just sitting here staring at this letter.
Found a taped-up envelope inside the wall when we pulled out the old radiator, addressed to whoever renovates next, from someone who apparently lived here in 1987.
kids ran straight into the new backyard the second we opened the door and started shrieking about the tree being perfect for a treehouse before a single box was off the truck.

We boarded the train home from Alderbury this morning, and I confess I wept rather more than I expected to, knowing it was very likely the last such journey my late husband and I ever planned together.

Forty-one years I've supported this club through relegations and worse, and when that header went in at the ninety-third minute I was on my feet screaming next to strangers, hugging every one of them.

The Farrells have been 'composting' directly against our shared fence for weeks now, and the stench that rolls over every time it rains is genuinely the foulest thing I've smelled come off a neighbour's yard.

Called the front office four times this week about the field trip permission slip mess, typed the same complaint email so many times I wore out the backspace key, and each time got a different person telling me a different rule that apparently only applies to my kid's class and nobody else's. Finally got the assistant principal on the phone and she put me on hold for eleven minutes before the call just dropped, so I called back and started the whole thing over from the beginning. Still no callback since.

Great news, everybody: the house next door is finally quiet. No more Frank out there at six a.m. every single Saturday running that ancient leaf blower like it owed him money, no more him leaning over the fence uninvited to tell me, in exhaustive detail, about some ballgame from 1987, no more finding a bag of tomatoes on my porch every August whether I wanted them or not because his garden 'got away from him again.' Really, a blessing. I get to keep my mornings to myself now. The funeral was Tuesday. His daughter asked if I wanted any of the garden tools since apparently he'd mentioned me by name in some list he kept of who should get what, which is a strange thing to learn about a man you only ever talked to across a chain-link fence for two decades. I said yes to the tomato cages, mostly because I didn't know how to say no standing in his driveway with his daughter, who looks exactly like him around the eyes, in a way I did not expect and have not stopped thinking about since. It's very restful over there now. Nobody's blower going off before I've had coffee. Nobody appearing at the fence uninvited with garden produce I never asked for and always somehow ended up eating all of anyway. I keep catching myself listening for it on Saturday mornings regardless, out of habit I suppose, and then remembering, and then just standing there in the kitchen a while longer than I mean to before I get on with the day.

Ran the same soup recipe twice this week, once with the fresh stock and once, out of laziness, with a bouillon cube substitution I fully expected to taste noticeably worse. Blind-tasted both batches against each other without labeling them beforehand. Three out of four testers picked the bouillon version as the better batch, and I could not, on a second tasting, tell which was which myself either.

My manager give the promotion to another person who start working only four months ago, even after he tell me many times this year that I am 'next in line' for it. I ask him why in the meeting yesterday and he just say 'it was a difficult decision' and change subject fast. I am very angry about this because I work extra hours for two years for this company and nobody say thank you for that, only excuses.

so my phone finally died for real this time, the old one, the one i never backed up because i kept saying i'd get to it. that's the one with literally every single photo of my dog on it from puppy to, well, all of it, none of it anywhere else. spent two hours last night googling data recovery services at 1am instead of just going to sleep like a normal person. haven't told anyone about it yet because saying it out loud sounds like a lot over a phone.

So the doctor said 'nothing to worry about' but also wants me back in for more bloodwork next week, and ever since that call I've reread the after-visit summary about four times looking for what she's not saying.
Movers broke a lamp and scuffed the stairs, minor stuff. Ran the new mortgage numbers again last night and I'm still not sure how we cover it if either contract doesn't renew in spring.

Hey so random but I was cleaning out my email and found the whole thread from when we were planning Dad's 60th, back when it was still just the four of us texting nonstop about restaurant options. Kind of wild how quiet the family group chat has gotten since everyone moved to different time zones. Type something in there every couple weeks now and mostly just get a thumbs up back, if anything at all. Not a big deal, just noticed it today I guess.

ok i need to vent for a sec. the guy next door had people over till 3am again last night. THIRD time this month. same bass line on repeat for like 4 hours straight, i could feel it thru my pillow. texted him at 1am asking to turn it down, he left me on read. saw him the next morning taking out trash and he just waved like nothing happened, didnt even bring it up. i brought it up. he said 'it wasnt that loud' which, no, i have a recording on my phone from my own bedroom that says otherwise. called the landlord today bc this is the third noise complaint ive filed since january and nothing ever actually happens, guy just gets a 'warning' and does it again two weeks later. my kid has school tomorrow and was up crying at 2am bc she couldnt sleep thru the noise, thats the part that actually gets me, not the bass, the fact that a 7 yr old is losing sleep over some guys 'get together.' landlord said hed 'look into it' which is what he said the last two times too so forgive me if im not holding my breath. at this point im tempted to just buy the loudest speaker i can find and see how he likes it at 7am on a sunday but obviously i wont bc im not trying to become the problem, i just want ONE uninterrupted nights sleep in my own apartment that i pay a lot of rent for.

kid went up for a header and came down wrong, just laid there on the pitch not moving for what felt like forever but was probably only 10 seconds. coach and ref both ran out immediately which made it worse somehow, not better. couldnt breathe right till i saw him sit up and give a thumbs up to the sideline. still shaking a bit tbh, cant really focus on the rest of the game now.

Mrs. Whiskers, who has studiously ignored every toy purchased for her across eleven years, spent the better part of twenty minutes this afternoon chasing a bottle cap around the kitchen floor. I set my newspaper down twice simply to watch. She has since returned to her usual post atop the radiator, as though nothing at all had occurred, and I find myself still glancing over at that bottle cap on the counter.
The crowd near the stage was pushing so hard I could not touch the ground with my feet for some seconds, and I was very scared we will get crushed before the music even start.
ugh my best friend just showed up at my door with tickets to the show i've wanted to see for two years without any warning at all, how dare she, guess i'm just never forgiving her for that one, rude.

Dad didn't answer his phone Tuesday morning. Called four times between eight and nine, no response. Called the neighbor, Mrs. Okafor, who said she'd check. She called back twenty minutes later saying his car was in the driveway but the front door was locked and the curtains were still closed at nine-fifteen, which is late for him. Called the non-emergency line. They said they could send someone but it would be at least forty minutes given call volume. Spent that forty minutes running through the worst version of Tuesday I could construct: fall, stroke, the stairs down to the basement he's not supposed to use alone since the hip surgery in March. Texted my sister. She was already driving, twenty minutes out. I couldn't do anything from four hundred miles away except keep calling a phone that kept ringing into nothing. Officer got there at 9:52. Called me back at 9:58 to say Dad was fine, hearing aid battery had died overnight so he'd slept through everything including four phone calls and a knock on the door. He was mildly annoyed about the fuss. I sat on my kitchen floor for a few minutes after that call before I could stand back up. Ordered him a second hearing aid charger for the nightstand that afternoon and a loud vibrating alarm clock, the kind made for people who can't hear a regular one. He says he doesn't need either. I'm sending them anyway.

The news say the storm will reach our city by tomorrow night and it is now category three, maybe stronger before it arrive. My husband is putting wood boards on all the windows since this morning but I can see his hands are not so steady when he is doing it. We have water bottles, some cans of food, flashlight, but not so much because the store was already very empty when we go there yesterday, many shelf completely bare. My daughter keep asking if the roof will be okay and I don't know really what to tell her that is true and also not scary for a seven year old to hear. Our neighbor decide to drive to his sister house two hours away this morning, he say the water here can rise very fast and he remember the last big storm eight years ago when the whole street was under water for three days. Now I am wondering if we should also go, but the roads maybe already very full of cars and it take much longer than normal, and I don't want to be stuck in the car during the worst part. I keep checking my phone every few minutes for new update even though I know the storm path is not going to change just because I am looking at it. Tonight we will sleep in the hallway, away from the windows, and I already put the important papers in a plastic bag by the door in case we need to leave fast.

Ok I need to rant for a sec lol. The app charged me twice for the same subscription this month, so I messaged support, and after 40 minutes of back and forth they told me to 'just wait 5-7 business days' for a refund that they agree is their mistake?? Like why am I fronting your billing error interest-free for a week, that's wild to me. Anyway sorry, needed to get that off my chest!

So we're up 2-1 with four minutes left in the league final, Jamie's team, the one they've practiced for since August, and the ref calls the tightest offside I have ever seen in my life on a play where their kid was clearly a full stride onside, waves it off, no VAR at this level obviously so that's just the final word, and the other team scores off the resulting free kick two minutes later to tie it and then wins it in extra time on penalties, and Jamie's coach tried to talk to the ref after the whistle just to ask which linesman made the call and got told to 'take it up with the league office' by a guy who was already halfway to his car. Filed the complaint form online that night, attached the video someone's dad filmed from the sideline that shows the offside line pretty clearly, got an auto-reply saying they'd 'review within 10 business days,' which, fine, except the season's already over by then so what exactly is there left to review. Jamie cried the whole ride home and kept asking why the ref didn't just look again, and I didn't have a real answer for her because I don't have one either, I just kept saying sometimes the calls don't go your way, which felt like a garbage thing to tell an eleven year old who did everything right for eight months straight.

I try to cook my grandmother rice dish again last night, the one with the orange spice she always use, but it never taste the same like when she make it. I call my mother to ask the recipe again even though I already have it write down from before. We talk for one hour about small things, not really about the recipe. After I hang up the phone I just sit in the kitchen for long time before I eat, food already getting cold on the table.
Oh wonderful, my dog leave me such a beautiful present on the pillow this morning, right where I put my face every night, thank you so much for that, exactly what I wanted to find at 6am.

I have not felt such an outpouring of gladness in a very long time as I did this past Sunday, when the whole family gathered under one roof for the first occasion in nearly six years. My daughter Margaret flew in from Rivermouth with her husband and the two children I had, until Sunday, only ever seen upon a screen; my son Peter drove up from the coast with his new fiancée, a delightfully cheerful young woman named Naomi whom I had heard a great deal about but never once met in person. We sat twelve at a table meant properly for eight, elbows knocking, three separate conversations happening at once across the length of the tablecloth, and I confess I spent a good portion of the afternoon simply watching rather than speaking, quite content to take in the noise of it all. My youngest grandchild, Theo, who is four and had apparently been told a great many stories about his grandfather, spent the better part of an hour attempting to teach me a card game whose rules changed, by my count, no fewer than six times over the course of play, and I lost every single round with what I hope was good grace. We took a photograph on the back steps just as the light was going, all twelve of us squeezed in somehow, and I have already had it printed and placed upon the mantel where I can see it each morning with my tea. It is a rare and precious thing, at my age, to have a house full again, if only for one afternoon, and I find myself still smiling about it three days on.

ok the cafeteria pulled something today that I need to talk about. opened my 'chicken' wrap and there was just. a long black hair baked into the tortilla itself, not on top, IN it, like it had been cooked in there. showed my friend and she almost threw up on the spot. went to complain and the lunch lady just shrugged and said 'happens sometimes' like that's a normal sentence to say out loud to a customer. brought my own lunch for the rest of the week, not risking it again.
Checked in for economy and somehow, to my complete shock, ended up boarding to find my pass now read seat 2A, first class, champagne already poured before push-back.

Yes, of course, this is exactly what I am expecting when I buy ticket for small local band in small venue with maybe two hundred people only. Totally normal Tuesday night, nothing special, just like every other concert I go before. So when the lights go down and instead of the small band, a man walk out who I recognize immediately because his face is on every music channel for twenty years, I am, sure, very calm about this, not surprised even one little bit. My friend next to me is also very calm, screaming into my ear so loud I cannot hear for maybe one minute after. He play for one full hour, just him, small stage, no big show, nothing, guitar and his voice only, like this is completely a normal Tuesday thing for a superstar to do in a room this small. Nobody in the room is filming much because everybody too busy standing there with mouth open, very typical reaction, very expected. After, we find out from the small band, the ones who actually sell tickets for this show, that they only know he was coming two days before, and he ask them himself if he can 'sit in' because he is visiting his old friend who lives in this city. Totally normal for a person of this fame to just quietly show up somewhere with two hundred seat. I walk out after and cannot remember where I park my car for ten minutes, which never happen to me before in my life, but sure, everything about tonight is very expected and very normal, exactly the concert I plan to see when I buy this ticket three weeks ago for twenty-two dollars.

Five-star dining experience review, truly:
- Reservation confirmed for 7pm, seated at 7:45, no apology offered
- Ordered the tasting menu, received the wrong courses twice, was told this was 'basically the same thing'
- Bill arrived with a mystery $40 'corkage fee' despite bringing no wine of our own
- Manager's solution to all of the above: a single free dessert, which also arrived at the wrong table first
Can't wait to recommend this place to literally everyone I have ever met.

I have lived in this county for seven and forty years and never once, not in all that time, have I seen hailstones the size of golf balls falling in the middle of June. They came down for perhaps six minutes, dented the roof of my car quite badly, and left the garden looking as though it had been through a hedge trimmer. My neighbour and I stood beneath the porch afterward simply staring at one another, entirely lost for words.

So this is going to sound like a lot over a dog, but stay with me for a second. We got Biscuit the same month I started my first real job out of college, which tells you how long ago that was, back when I was twenty-three and living in that terrible apartment above the laundromat that always smelled like fabric softener no matter what. He's been through two apartments, one house, one divorce, and about four different haircuts of my own that I'd rather not revisit, and through all of it he was just there, this consistent, ridiculous presence who greeted every single homecoming like I'd been gone for a decade instead of an hour. Lately, though, he doesn't really get up to greet me at the door anymore. Takes him a minute to work his back legs into standing, and I've started timing my entrances so I have a second to compose myself before he looks up at me, because something about watching him try gets me every single time. The vet says it's just age, nothing acute, nothing to rush into any decisions about, which I'm grateful for, genuinely, but I've also started doing this thing where I take a picture of him basically every day now, on the couch, in the yard, wherever, because some part of my brain has started keeping a record I'm not ready to think too hard about the reason for. He's thirteen this year. I know what thirteen means for a dog his size. I'm just not there yet, mentally, so for now I'm taking a lot of pictures and trying not to do the math out loud.

Okay funny pet update: we always figured our tabby Pepper was, at best, food-motivated and lazy, zero interest in anything that wasn't her bowl. So today I'm sitting on the floor doing paperwork and she walks over, sniffs the open folder, and starts very deliberately pulling pages out one by one and lining them up next to her like she's sorting them. I've had this cat six years. I did not know this was a thing she could even conceive of doing, and I still don't have an explanation for it.

Update log:
- Powered up the old router for the first time in three years
- It still had our previous address's wifi name saved
- Did not expect that after two moves
